originality.rationale: Substantive comparison, not timestamp: Balister et al. (arXiv:1907.09464) is existential (constants delta,Delta for all n, no witness, no merit, no per-length table); Jedwab-Katz-Schmidt (arXiv:1205.0626) is asymptotic skew merit (>6.34 families, no finite-length certificate, no sup-norm); Brest-Boskovic (arXiv:2011.00068) is heuristic best-known skew merit for lengths 201-303 (disjoint window, no optimality, no sup-norm); Boskovic-Herzog-Brest (arXiv:2210.15962) is a stochastic GPU solver for L=121-223 explicitly unable to guarantee optimality, no sup-norm. arXiv all-fields searches for joint skew Pareto flatness-merit and for optimal skew N=33 returned no results. No source publishes an exhaustive joint (F,M) Pareto frontier or frozen-rectangle verdict at N=33 with sup-norm enclosure. Internal overlap check concurs: SCOPE027 (mean demerit n=3..21) differs in length, statistic, and route. The joint frontier plus exclusion is therefore new and not mechanically implied.

decisive_checks: Executed inputs/artifacts/verify.py: VERIFY_OK (exact census, odd-lag lemma, reversal pairs, DFT replay, Bernstein factor, exclusion, Pareto domination).
Independent stdlib direct-DFT replay of 20 random gmax_all.json entries: all agree within 5e-10 (tolerance 1e-6).
Hand-checked merit fractions: 1089/176=99/16=6.1875; 1089/240=363/80=4.5375; 1089/256=4.25390625; F>=6<=>E<=90.75 so only E=88 qualifies given 8-divisibility.

Verified Bernstein enclosure direction: x_up=3.14159266/1024 upper-bounds pi/1024, cos(x)>=1-x^2/2 gives rigorous f_up; margins (exclusion gap 0.0576, Pareto ratio 1.0106) exceed floating slack by >2000x.
Confirmed scope honesty: DRAFT limits claims to skew subspace with a0=+1, stipulated rectangle, Bernstein (not algebraic) upper bounds.
residual_risks: Lower-bound flatness values rest on floating-point DFT evaluation; gap to threshold (0.0576) exceeds any plausible double-precision error by >6 orders, but not a formal interval-arithmetic proof.
Bare number E*=88/F*=6.1875 for skew N=33 could in principle appear in an obscure LABS table; the joint (F,M) frontier with sup-norm enclosure has no such prior and carries the novelty.
Bernstein grid bound is a standard estimate applied correctly here, but upper flatness intervals are enclosures, not exact sup-norm maximizations.
